---
title: "Local Operator Environment"
execute:
  eval: false
engine: markdown
---

direnv is an optional command-line convenience for a Manual operator. It is
not part of the scientific execution environment: the container runner starts
with a clean environment, and Spack plus the container image define the R ABI,
system libraries, and reproducible package installation.

The generated .envrc only helps an operator locate this checkout and invoke the
isolated Manual render with a memorable command. It does not contain data
locations, credentials, release parameters, library paths, or scientific
dependencies.

::: {.manual-prereq title="Enable The Local Convenience Layer"}

Install direnv, ensure its shell hook is enabled, then run direnv allow from
the repository root after materializing the file. Re-run direnv allow whenever
its contents change.

:::

::: {.manual-procedure .emit-generic file="{{ emit.project_root }}/.envrc" title="Materialize The Local direnv Contract"}

~~~bash
# This file is generated from notebooks/infrastructure/10_page-direnv.qmd.
# It is intentionally local and ignored by Git.

export PROJECT_DIR="$(CDPATH= cd -- "$(dirname -- "$BASH_SOURCE")" && pwd)"
PATH_add "$PROJECT_DIR/scripts"
~~~

:::

## What this does—and does not—provide

This file deliberately does not set PATH, SPACK_VIEW, LD_LIBRARY_PATH, or
PKG_CONFIG_PATH. Those variables cannot configure a clean container invocation
and would blur the boundary between host-side engineering and scientific work.
The runner and image establish the scientific environment inside Singularity.
direnv adds only the existing generated scripts directory to PATH; it does not
create a function, alias, shim, or additional implementation file.

Use the existing isolated-render command without its path for the normal Manual
workflow:

~~~sh
render-isolated --profile authoring
render-isolated --profile emit
~~~

For Slurm jobs, scripts, or systems without direnv, invoke
scripts/render-isolated directly. That wrapper remains the one portable,
auditable implementation; direnv only removes its path from an interactive
shell.

::: {.manual-check title="Verify The Activated Environment"}

~~~sh
direnv allow
test "$PROJECT_DIR" = "$PWD"
command -v quarto
type render-isolated
~~~

:::
